D1: a VariableDefinition's declared type had NO relationship, while a field return type, an argument type and an input field type all had one — so `$c: Color` said nothing about `Color` and `returnType`/`rawType` carried the fact as a string where every sibling fact is an edge

D2: an enum member named in a VALUE position (an input field default, an argument default, a variable default, an executable field argument, a directive argument) was recorded only as an opaque string in `defaultValue`, so the enum member was a declared symbol that NOTHING ever referenced

D3: the DirectiveDefinition branch emitted the `@name` symbol with `parameters` and then NO relationships at all, so `directive @auth(requires: Role = ADMIN)` said nothing about `Role` — and a directive's argument type was the only declared type in the language with no edge to it

D4: the enum-value edge is qualified `Enum.RED` only where the document itself states the type, and bare `RED` where it does not. Dropping the qualification collapses `Color.RED` to `RED` on every input field, argument and variable default — the two spellings are different facts and the store resolves them by different strategies

D5: the `EnumValue` node appears BOTH as a declaration (`EnumValueDefinition > EnumValue`, already a symbol with a `contains` edge) and as a reference (`Value > EnumValue`). Keying on the node type alone would publish a declaration as a reference to itself
results.equivalentByConstruction: NOT separable at the current call sites, and the reason is structural rather than convenient. All SIX call sites pass a `DefaultValue` or a `Value` node: four pass `DefaultValue` (whose only child is `Value`) and two pass `Value` directly. An `EnumValue` reached from either subtree therefore ALWAYS has a `Value` parent, so `n.parent?.type === "Value"` is true for every node the collector can reach, and dropping it changes no output on any input. The test is a CONTRACT on the helper — "return references, not declarations" — and it becomes load-bearing the moment a call site passes anything wider (a whole `Directive`, a `Definition`, a selection set). Declared equivalent rather than quietly deleted, because the guard is correct and a future call site is exactly when it would matter. What IS pinned at the call sites is D2 (the collector returning nothing) and D4 (the qualification), both caught.

results.defect: E1: the iterative `findDescendant` pushed children FORWARD, so it popped the LAST child first and returned a different first match — a different NamedType, and therefore a different type reference. A right answer for the wrong reason, and invisible to any fixture that has one clause
results.equivalentByConstruction: DERIVABLE from the grammar, not merely unobserved by the fixtures. `findDescendant` is called on two shapes and both admit exactly one match. (1) A `Type` subtree: `Type: NamedType | ListType | NonNullType`, `ListType: '[' Type ']'`, `NonNullType: (NamedType | ListType) '!' | Type '!'` — by induction a Type subtree contains EXACTLY ONE NamedType, so the order in which children are examined cannot change the result. (2) A `DirectiveLocation`: `DirectiveLocation: ExecutableDirectiveLocation | TypeSystemDirectiveLocation`, a CHOICE with exactly one child. So pushing children forward instead of backward returns the same node on every input this grammar can produce. The reverse-order push is kept because it makes the helper correct for a predicate that CAN match more than once — `collectNamedTypes` is that predicate, and it is a different function — and because a grammar change adding a second NamedType to a Type would otherwise silently start returning the wrong one.

results.defect: E2: `ImplementsInterfaces` and `UnionMemberTypes` are LEFT-recursive, so `A & B & C` nests; collecting only the first NamedType silently dropped every clause after the first, which is the defect the pre-pass exists to prevent

E3: an `EnumValue` in a value position is a leaf — there is nothing below it. Descending into it is harmless today, but the loop form uses `continue` where the recursion used `return`, and `continue` that descended would make the walk unbounded on a cyclic-looking shape
results.equivalentByConstruction: The grammar says `EnumValue: Name` — an EnumValue node's only content is a `Name`, and a `Name` is never an `EnumValue`. So descending into a matched EnumValue cannot find another EnumValue, and the collector returns the same list on every input this grammar can produce. Kept as `continue` (do not descend) anyway, because it states the intent — an enum value in a value position is a LEAF — and because the loop form needs an explicit decision there where the recursion got it from `return`.

The unnamed-operation identity numbers the operations of a DOCUMENT, and the counter lives on the analyzer instance. A pooled worker reuses one instance across files, so without the per-`analyze` reset the second file's only unnamed operation publishes as `<stem>::operation_2`. Not catchable by this harness or by run-fixtures.ts, because BOTH construct a fresh analyzer per file (score.mts:77 does `new Analyzer()` inside the loop, and a fixture is one file) and therefore start the counter at 0 regardless. Verified: this mutant SURVIVES the fixture suite 5/5 and is caught by probe/analyzer-reuse.mts, which reuses one instance and exits 1.
